prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words; policy-focused)

Health and care
- NHS: Additional revenue spend in England rising from £8bn in year one to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Priorities: faster GP access, same-day urgent GP access, universal NHS dentistry, waiting list reduction, staff pay uplifts. Primary care: +£1.5bn/yr by 2030; £2bn capital. Public health: +£1.5bn to restore 2015/16 levels. Dentistry: new NHS contract and investment reaching £3bn/yr by 2030. National Cancer Plan; evidence-based mental health access within 28 days; counsellor in every school; assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/yr investment; career structure and improved pay; anti-exploitation visa reforms; disability benefits +5%; SEND transport duty; children’s social care +£3bn.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/year; end Right to Buy; empower rent controls; end no-fault evictions; tenant dispute boards. Retrofit programme: £29bn for home insulation to EPC B over five years, £9bn for low‑carbon heat, £7bn for heat adaptation, £4bn for public buildings; mandate Passivhaus-equivalent, solar and heat pumps in new homes; raise PRS efficiency standards; bring empty homes into use.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax rising over 10 years. Targets by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore wind, 100GW solar; aim wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; end de-facto ban on onshore wind; community ownership thresholds; expand grid, storage, interconnectors; regulate biofuels, end imported biomass subsidies; cease new nuclear and phase out existing plants; green hydrogen for industry.

Economy, tax and public ownership
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr: power, retrofit, rail (£30bn), public transport (£7bn), active travel (£6bn), industry decarbonisation, water/sewage, nationalising water and Big 5 energy retailers. Bring rail, water, Big 5 energy retailers into public ownership. R&D +£30bn over five years; circular economy, right to repair, 10‑year warranties. Tax: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and pension relief; business windfall taxes; VAT changes (reduce hospitality/arts; raise on financial services/private education); carbon tax £120/t rising to up to £500/t. Strengthen HMRC; borrow to invest with inflation-aware constraint.

Work and welfare
- Repeal recent anti-union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; minimum wage £15/hour for all ages (small business offset via higher Employment Allowance); 10:1 pay ratio target; day‑one rights; gig workers classified as workers; progress toward four-day week. Welfare: +£40/week to UC and legacy benefits; end five-week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; disability benefits +5%; carers +10%; retain real-terms pension uprating; end sanctions; long‑term UBI goal.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; protect 30% land and seas by 2030; rewet peat; urban biodiversity measures; public ownership of water; DEFRA +£1.5bn. Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics); ban snaring/lead ammo; badger vaccination over cull. Farming: nearly triple support; link payments to soil health and reduced pesticides; expand horticulture and mixed farming; strengthen supply-chain fairness; universal free school meals and breakfast (to Year 6); food education and local food partnerships.

Education
- Free, inclusive public education; abolish Ofsted and high‑stakes testing; £8bn schools (incl. £2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/yr for buildings/RAAC; bring academies under councils; VAT on private school fees (SEN exempt); SEND +£5bn; Sure Start +£1.4bn/yr; extend funded childcare to 35 hours from nine months (sector negotiation); Sixth form +£3bn; FE/lifelong +£12bn; restore EMA; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Transport
- Rail/bus subsidies to £10bn/yr by end of parliament; £19bn over five years for public transport and electrification; public ownership of rail; free buses for under‑18s; £2.5bn/yr for cycling/walking; oppose new roads; fuel duty escalator, road pricing later; end new ICE sales by 2027 and road use by 2035; scrappage up to £5bn/yr; weight‑based road tax; default 20mph. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights under 3‑hour rail; no airport expansion; carbon tax on kerosene.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Fair Politics Act: repeal voter ID; restore Electoral Commission powers; proportional representation; party state funding; lobbying/think‑tank transparency; votes at 16; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; local govt +£5bn/yr; uphold HRA/ECHR; scrap recent protest laws; support gender self‑ID. Migration: end hostile environment; remove spouse income rules; safe routes; allow work during asylum; end NRPF and 10‑year route; limit detention; voting rights for visa‑holders; split Home Office functions; reduce fees to cost; NHS access.

Justice and policing
- End routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; diversity fitness assessments; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; decriminalise personal drug possession with diversion; VAWG strategy, make misogyny a hate crime; invest £11bn over parliament to restore MoJ, courts, legal aid; fund youth services.

Foreign policy/Europe/defence
- Support Ukraine; strengthen international law; seek to rejoin EU (customs union first), restore free movement and Erasmus; aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss and Damage; debt relief; ecocide law. Sign TPNW, cancel Trident, dismantle nukes; remain in NATO while advocating reforms (No First Use, defensive focus).
